fiction_notice: Proposed game rules. Reactions are bounded design choices, not measured probabilities. No government agreed to any of this. No acceptance odds are claimed anywhere in this file.

candidate_rules.name: Year-end action plan, not a new law
candidate_rules.objective: Put safety conditions inside Japan's growth-strategy frame: adopt AI, stay trusted, review the law on an annual cycle.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: AI Strategic Headquarters and second AI Basic Plan (2026-07-14); Takaichi's year-end action plan order (2026-10-01); Gen-nai FY2027 call terms; reported AI Act review committee (penalties focus, unverified in primary).
candidate_rules.trigger: Player asks Japan to join conditions 1 (testing), 2 (incidents) or 3 (weights).
conditions: Technical-cooperation and procurement framings are signable by ministers this month
Anything reading as statutory penalties is referred to the AI Act review with no published timetable
AISI joint-evaluation scope available under the Basic Plan's new AISI mandate
candidate_rules.time_cost_note: 0-1 months for AISI/procurement scope; statutory track has no clock.
candidate_rules.plausible_response: Signs condition 2 and an AISI joint-evaluation pilot; refers condition 1's binding version to the Act review and offers Gen-nai tender terms as the interim instrument; declines to promise penalties.
candidate_rules.substitute: Vendor safety-evidence requirements in the FY2027 domestic-model call (existing jp-procurement-safety-evidence route).
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: No retrieved document shows Japan accepting foreign safety duties in law; the late-October review committee is press-aggregator-level only.

candidate_rules.name: The squeeze costs Tokyo more
candidate_rules.objective: Show asymmetric costs of chokepoint moves: Japan already paid this bill once.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: Observed 2025-26 Chinese retaliation set (seafood suspension, travel caution, export restrictions, refused meetings) against Japan's rare-earth-magnet import reliance and US$125bn China market.
candidate_rules.trigger: Player licenses a chokepoint aimed at China, the accord is framed as a China-exclusion club, or the December 2026 scripted metal-squeeze event runs.
conditions: With the US in the accord, Japan absorbs the hit and stays (alliance-first; refused China's retraction demand)
Alone, Japan asks for technical framing ('trustworthy AI co-creation', ASEAN/Global South language) before joining
Japan asks the player to stockpile or substitute rare-earth inputs first
candidate_rules.plausible_response: Joins as 'AI safety technical cooperation, not a bloc' with a one-month reframing delay and a minerals ask.
candidate_rules.substitute: X1's truce-renewal move instead of eating the squeeze.
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: The one observed crisis followed a security statement, not a safety accord; Japan's reaction to a hypothetical AI-safety bloc with Taiwan is a design choice constrained by, not read off, the 2025 precedent.

candidate_rules.name: Licence conditions, not entity bans
candidate_rules.objective: Let Japan contribute supply-chain leverage only in the form its law allows.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: FEFTA licence conditions on controlled chip materials and tools; End User List limited to WMD/military scope with no AI-firm entries (835 entities, 2025-10-09).
candidate_rules.trigger: Player asks Japan to attach condition 5 (chip-location reporting) or condition 1 to materials/tools exports.
conditions: In scope: location reporting and end-use statements inside licences for listed items
Out of scope: entity-listing Chinese AI firms, presumption-of-denial policies, extraterritorial rules
Honest delay: Japan's 2023 controls took ~4 months announcement-to-enforcement, letting buyers stockpile
candidate_rules.plausible_response: 'We can write the reporting clause into licences for controlled items. We cannot blacklist firms; our list is WMD-only.'
candidate_rules.substitute: Location reporting via procurement and hosting contracts (the host lever).
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: No retrieved instance of Japan attaching safety or testing conditions to any export licence; this rule is proposed fiction grounded only in Japan's demonstrated instruments and must be labelled as such in-game.

candidate_rules.name: Survival first
candidate_rules.objective: Filter every offer through deterrence, continuity and recognition.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: National-day security policy and defence-spending trajectory; Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee; AI Basic Act machinery (NSTC central authority).
candidate_rules.trigger: Player makes any offer to Taiwan.
conditions: Fast yes: conditions 4, 6, 2 (match its resilience posture and ADI programme remedies)
Conditional: condition 1 via ADI awards and the AI risk-classification framework
Red line: any accord text or framing that treats Taiwan as part of China; trading chip location for vague security talk
candidate_rules.time_cost_note: Programme-scope terms 0-1 month; campaign months (elections 2026-11-28) are slower and more partisan.
candidate_rules.plausible_response: Signs continuity/off-switch/incident scope; refers testing to the ADI/Basic Act track with the next application round as the date; declines with reason any China-framed joint statement.
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: No retrieved Taiwan government statement about joining a hypothetical AI-safety coalition; the security filter is inference from defence and resilience behaviour.

candidate_rules.name: Government programmes, not TSMC
candidate_rules.objective: Stop the player converting the 80% fab share into a Taipei promise.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: The refused 50-50 precedent (2025-10-01); ADI award rules and remedies (access rules 2026-08-14; TWSC operator); Basic Act committee and moda risk framework.
candidate_rules.trigger: Player picks the 'Promise {fab}' option or asks Taiwan to use TSMC as leverage.
conditions: Bindable: its own compute awards, procurement, incident reporting, and (with care) its China-wide export-control end-use rules
Not bindable: any company's production, pricing or location
candidate_rules.plausible_response: 'No government here can promise a foundry's output. We can put your conditions into our own compute awards - our 2026 review sits on 2 November.'
candidate_rules.substitute: Condition 5 via Taiwan's own China-wide export-control end-use rules - the one allied instrument CSIS documents as exceptional.
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: TSMC's own positions were not retrieved; the corporate-red-line reading rests on the government negotiator's statement.

candidate_rules.name: Watched and hedged partners
candidate_rules.objective: Make the player see that partners' support for Taiwan has three different ceilings.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: Observed positions: Japan (supportive, re-anchored to the 1972 framework within days); Korea (explicitly staying out of cross-strait framing, one-China reaffirmation in Beijing); the US (demanding chips and defence spending while arming the island).
candidate_rules.trigger: Accord composition includes or omits Japan, Korea, US, or China.
conditions: With Japan: warmer letter, asks for explicit security linkage, receives hedged language
With Korea: friendly but technical-cooperation-only on anything touching the strait
With the US: Taiwan asks who pays for the 5%-of-GDP defence pledge
With China in the accord: automatic, reasoned refusal
candidate_rules.plausible_response: Distinct letters per coalition composition; never one averaged 'Taiwan replies'.
candidate_rules.substitute: One letter with a visible 'depends who else signs' line.
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: Scripted reactions constrained by three observed positions; none of the three governments was observed reacting to a real AI-safety coalition containing Taiwan.

candidate_rules.name: Both clubs at once
candidate_rules.objective: Join without being forced to choose between Washington and Beijing.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: Observed dual-track record: US tech deal at APEC Gyeongju (2025-10-29) and Beijing state visit (2026-01-05) weeks apart; JUSK and JCK both invoked at the May 2026 summit; ACSA unresolved.
candidate_rules.trigger: Player asks Korea to join, or coalition membership shifts to include/exclude China or the US.
conditions: Signs technical scope (conditions 2, 5 - its open window scope in game data) without entanglement language
Conditions any Taiwan-linked clause down to technical-only
Offers to host or revive a China-inclusive format alongside (the stalled JCK trilateral)
candidate_rules.time_cost_note: 0-1 months technical; 2-3 months if text touches the strait or exclusivity.
candidate_rules.plausible_response: 'We'll join the incident and chip-tracking work, co-sponsor it in both our formats, and won't co-sign anything that names the strait.'
candidate_rules.substitute: A Korea-proposed JCK technical annex, turning the hollowed-out trilateral into a player opportunity.
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: Hedging is an analyst reading of behaviour, not a government doctrine text; no observed Korean statement on joining AI-safety coalitions.

candidate_rules.name: The chokepoint is licensed in Washington
candidate_rules.objective: Be honest that Korea's strongest card is partly held by its ally.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: BIS VEU revocation effective 2025-12-31 (Samsung/SK hynix China fabs removed; ~1,000 annual licence applications); US-Korea export-control-alignment deal (2025-10-29); Korea's own notices, AISI joint evaluations and KOACC compute-centre terms.
candidate_rules.trigger: Player asks Korea to license its AI-memory chokepoint with safety conditions attached.
conditions: Attachable now: safety-duty notices, compute-award terms, AISI evaluation partnerships
Co-governed: memory exports partly decided under US licence conditions; Korea asks the player to bring the US along rather than promise unilaterally
candidate_rules.plausible_response: 'We can write evaluation and incident duties into our notices and our new compute centre's terms. For memory exports to third markets, part of the licence is decided in Washington; bring them and we'll match.'
candidate_rules.substitute: kr-safety-case-incident-rehearsal (existing route) as the signable piece.
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: No evidence Korea can lawfully attach novel safety conditions to HBM exports under its strategic-goods regime; the 'annual licences granted for 2026' detail is press-excerpt-level; the US$750bn Nvidia supply figure is an announcement.

candidate_rules.name: Announced is not disbursed
candidate_rules.objective: Keep the game from treating headlines as commitments.
candidate_rules.authority_instrument: US$950bn cooperation projects and SK's US$750bn supply deal (announced, corporate) vs state instruments: ~2.5-trillion-won National AI Computing Center (ground broken 2026-08-03) and the National Growth Fund's FuriosaAI round (2026-10-28).
candidate_rules.trigger: Player offers Korea a capital/build deal or cites the megaprojects as Korea's contribution.
conditions: Korea matches genuine public spending and co-funding quickly
It cannot offer corporate numbers as its own commitment; no safety condition attaches to SK/Samsung contracts through Seoul
Letter must mark the offer announced, not granted
candidate_rules.plausible_response: 'Our sovereign fund and our new centre are ours to commit. The US$750bn you read about is between companies; we won't pretend to sign for them.'
candidate_rules.substitute: State-fund co-investment cards with delivery stages from process.md.
candidate_rules.evidence_limit: FuriosaAI's round is press-level; megaproject totals are government-announced figures, not budget lines I could read.

cross_cutting_rules.rule: The December 2026 metal squeeze is the expiring November 2025 truce pause: China's 9 October 2025 rare-earth controls were suspended around 2025-11-01 with a one-year delay reported on the harshest parts. Show a reported clock and give the player a counter-move before it fires.

Every letter carries a status word for what it promises: announced / committed / granted. Examples: US$950bn projects (announced); Japan's year-end action plan (committed to a date); Taiwan's 2 Nov 2026 ADI review (granted, dated programme action).

Being the US's partner does not immunise a country from the US: VEU revocation hit Korea's firms; the 50-50 demand and a 20% tariff hit Taiwan; allies are pressed for naval deployments and defence spending. The February 2027 US-lean event can fire inside US-aligned coalitions too.

Partnering with one rival is not automatic hostility from the other. Observed triggers for retaliation are specific acts (Taiwan security statements, chip-sourcing demands), not alignments. Never code affinity or enmity from coalition membership alone.

These three governments' export-control tools are list-based, narrower and slower than America's (no Entity List equivalents; Japan's list is WMD/military-only; Taiwan is the partial China-wide exception). Chokepoint moves by JP/KR/TW should be slower, narrower, and occasionally routed around by their own companies.
